title: Static Equilibrium and Torque
seo_title: Physics 12: Static Equilibrium and Torque Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
short_title: torque, centre of mass and equilibrium
standard_text: Forces can cause linear and circular motion: torque, the conditions for static equilibrium, centre of mass, and force components. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Physics 12)
meta_desc: Free Physics 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): torque, centre of mass and equilibrium. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: In equilibrium, the net force and the net torque are zero.
body_html:
How to think about it

Torque is the turning effect of a force: τ = rF sin θ, where r is the distance from the pivot. For an object to be in static equilibrium, the net force is zero (forces balance) and the net torque about any point is zero (clockwise torques = counterclockwise torques).

The centre of mass is the point where the whole weight seems to act; an object is stable when its centre of mass is above its base. Forces at an angle are resolved into components to apply the equilibrium conditions.

Example

A 200 N child sits 1.5 m from a seesaw pivot. How far away must a 300 N child sit to balance?

200 × 1.5 = 300 × d

Answer: 1.0 m

Example

Why is a long wrench easier to use?

τ = rF

Answer: a larger r gives more torque

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the sin θ when the force is at an angle.
  • Measuring r from the wrong point.
  • Thinking equilibrium means no forces act.
